title: Am Automaten
desc: A ticket, a track and eight minutes
setting: Zurich airport, underground, with a suitcase and no idea where track seven is.

steps.speaker: Der Automat
steps.en: Where would you like to travel to?

options.feedback: Nach for a town or a country. Short is right, it is a machine.
It works. Nach Luzern is the whole answer.
Zu goes to people and to buildings. Towns and countries take nach.

options.en: Yes, I am finished. Go ahead.
options.feedback: Bitte on its own is the whole of "go ahead". It does a great deal of work in this language.
Honest and fine if you are not. He will wait.
True, possibly, but bare. Einen Moment costs you nothing.

steps.speaker: Eine Frau am Perron
steps.en: Grüezi. Are you looking for something?

options.es: Ja, wo ist Gleis sieben, bitte?
options.en: Yes, where is track seven, please?
options.feedback: Gleis is the numbered track. She will point, or she will walk you there.

options.es: Wo ist der Zug nach Luzern?
options.en: Where is the train to Luzern?
options.feedback: She will understand and answer with a track number, which is what you needed anyway.
Bahnsteig is the German German word. Here it is the Perron, and the number on the board is the Gleis.

steps.speaker: Die Frau am Perron
steps.es: Dort unten, dann rechts. Sie haben noch vier Minuten.
steps.en: Down there, then right. You have four minutes left.

options.feedback: She gave you directions and a warning. Merci vielmal is the right size of thank you for both.
Fine. She did rather more than a plain merci.

options.es: Vier Minuten? Das ist zu wenig!
options.en: Four minutes? That is not enough!
options.feedback: Here four minutes is four minutes. She has told you it is enough by telling you the number.
